This creates vendor lock-in and forces costly rewrites when a chosen framework becomes limiting or unmaintained.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAgentML is the universal language for agents, inspired by the success of HTML for the web.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto\" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=\"AgentML : Agent Frameworks  =  HTML : Web Browsers\"\u003e\u003cpre class=\"notranslate\"\u003e\u003ccode\u003eAgentML : Agent Frameworks  =  HTML : Web Browsers\n\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/pre\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eJust as HTML lets you write content once and have it render in any browser, AgentML lets you define your agent's behavior once and run it anywhere. This is achieved by building on the battle-tested \u003ca href=\"https://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/\" rel=\"nofollow\"\u003eW3C SCXML standard\u003c/a\u003e, a formal model for state machines that has been proven for over 20 years in complex industrial systems.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eThis provides two primary paths for execution:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eNative Execution (Recommended)\u003c/strong\u003e: Run agents with \u003cstrong\u003e\u003ccode\u003eagentmlx\u003c/code\u003e\u003c/strong\u003e, the reference runtime built in Go/WASM. It's designed for high performance and portability.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eTransformation (Planned)\u003c/strong\u003e: To integrate with existing ecosystems, we are planning roadmap.\u003c/strong\u003e\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eBy separating behavior from runtime, your agents outlive framework <blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><strong>🚧 Early Alpha - Building in Public</strong></p>
<p dir="auto">AgentML is in early alpha and being built openly with the community. The vision is ambitious, the foundation is solid, but many features are still in development. Join us in shaping the future of agent standards.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>📋 This Repository:</strong> Contains the AgentML language specification, documentation, and examples. For runtime implementations and namespace packages, see:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong><a href="https://github.com/agentflare-ai/agentmlx">agentmlx</a></strong> - Reference runtime (Go/WASM) <strong>NOT YET RELEASED</strong></li>
<li><strong><a href="https://github.com/agentflare-ai/agentml-go">agentml-go</a></strong> - Go namespace implementations (Gemini, Ollama, Memory, etc.)</li>
</ul>
</blockquote>
<hr>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">The Vision: A Universal Language for AI Agents</h2><a id="user-content-the-vision-a-universal-language-for-ai-agents" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: The Vision: A Universal Language for AI Agents" href="#the-vision-a-universal-language-for-ai-agents"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The AI agent landscape is fragmented and accelerating, with new frameworks appearing weekly. This creates vendor lock-in and forces costly rewrites when a chosen framework becomes limiting or unmaintained.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>AgentML is the universal language for agents, inspired by the success of HTML for the web.</strong></p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="AgentML : Agent Frameworks  =  HTML : Web Browsers"><pre class="notranslate"><code>AgentML : Agent Frameworks  =  HTML : Web Browsers
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Just as HTML lets you write content once and have it render in any browser, AgentML lets you define your agent's behavior once and run it anywhere. This is achieved by building on the battle-tested <a href="https://www.w3.org/TR/scxml/" rel="nofollow">W3C SCXML standard</a>, a formal model for state machines that has been proven for over 20 years in complex industrial systems.</p>
<p dir="auto">This provides two primary paths for execution:</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li><strong>Native Execution (Recommended)</strong>: Run agents with <strong><code>agentmlx</code></strong>, the reference runtime built in Go/WASM. It's designed for high performance and portability.</li>
<li><strong>Transformation (Planned)</strong>: To integrate with existing ecosystems, we are planning transformers to convert AgentML into other popular frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI, n8n, and more. <strong>This feature is not yet implemented but is a key part of our roadmap.</strong></li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">By separating behavior from runtime, your agents outlive framework trends.</p>

<p dir="auto">To run AgentML files (<code>.aml</code>), you need the <code>agentmlx</code> runtime. Choose the installation method for your platform:</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Core Concepts</h2><a id="user-content-core-concepts" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Core Concepts" href="#core-concepts"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">AgentML uses SCXML state machines to define <strong>deterministic behavior</strong>, moving beyond prompt-only approaches where behavior is emergent and unpredictable.</p>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>State Machines</strong>: Explicitly define valid states, transitions, and the agent's lifecycle. This enables formal verification and testing.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Schema-Guided Events</strong>: LLM outputs are constrained to structured JSON events validated against schemas using the <code>event:schema</code> attribute. This ensures reliability and type safety.</p>
<blockquote>
<p dir="auto"><g-emoji class="g-emoji" alias="warning">⚠️</g-emoji> <strong>Work in Progress</strong>: Event schema validation and external schema loading (<code>import</code> directive) are in active development. APIs and features may change as we refine the implementation based on community feedback.</p>
</blockquote>
<p dir="auto">The <code>event:schema</code> attribute on a transition provides JSON schema validation for an event. <strong>It is critical to include <code>description</code> fields</strong> at both the schema and property level, as these descriptions are the primary way to guide LLMs in generating correct event data.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>With Descriptions (Good):</strong></p>
</li>
</ol>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
        "type": "object",
      "description": "User intent to perform a flight-related action (search, book, update, cancel)",
        "properties": {
          "action": {
          "type": "string",
            "enum": ["search", "book", "update", "cancel"],
          "description": "The specific action: search for flights, book a new flight, etc."
          },
          "details": {
            "type": "object",
          "description": "Flight-specific information extracted from user message",
            "properties": {
              "from": {
                "type": "string",
              "description": "Departure location: city name or airport code (e.g., 'New York' or 'JFK')"
            }
          }
        }
  }
}"><pre>{
        <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>object<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
      <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>User intent to perform a flight-related action (search, book, update, cancel)<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"properties"</span>: {
          <span class="pl-ent">"action"</span>: {
          <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>string<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
            <span class="pl-ent">"enum"</span>: [<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>search<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>book<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>update<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>cancel<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>],
          <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>The specific action: search for flights, book a new flight, etc.<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
          },
          <span class="pl-ent">"details"</span>: {
            <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>object<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
          <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Flight-specific information extracted from user message<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
            <span class="pl-ent">"properties"</span>: {
              <span class="pl-ent">"from"</span>: {
                <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>string<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
              <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Departure location: city name or airport code (e.g., 'New York' or 'JFK')<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
            }

<ol start="3" dir="auto">
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Efficient Token Usage</strong>: The runtime provides the LLM with a "snapshot" of the current state, datamodel, and available events. This context allows prompts to be minimal, and the static parts (the agent's SCXML definition) can be cached by the LLM provider, reducing token consumption.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Decomposition</strong>: Complex agents can be broken down into smaller, reusable state machines using the <code><invoke></code> tag. This is ideal for managing complexity and sharing components like authentication or payment processing.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p dir="auto"><strong>Compiler-Inspired Validation</strong>: To ensure reliability, especially when agents are building other agents, AgentML includes a powerful validation system. Inspired by the Rust compiler (<code>rustc</code>), it provides detailed, actionable error messages that help developers (and other agents) pinpoint issues quickly and achieve a high success rate when generating AgentML documents.</p>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Schema References with <code>import</code></h3><a id="user-content-schema-references-with-import" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Schema References with import" href="#schema-references-with-import"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">To keep agent files clean and promote reuse, schemas can be defined in external JSON or YAML files (including OpenAPI specs) and loaded with an <code>import</code> directive. The runtime intelligently detects the file type.</p>
<p dir="auto">This enables schema reuse via <strong>JSON Pointer (RFC 6901)</strong> references with namespace prefixes.</p>
<p dir="auto"><strong>schemas/events.json:</strong></p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-json notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="{
  "components": {
    "schemas": {
      "FlightRequest": {
  "type": "object",
        "description": "Schema for a flight-related request.",
  "properties": {
            "action": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/FlightAction" }
        }
      },
      "FlightAction": {
      "type": "string",
          "enum": ["search", "book", "cancel"]
      }
    }
  }
}"><pre>{
  <span class="pl-ent">"components"</span>: {
    <span class="pl-ent">"schemas"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"FlightRequest"</span>: {
  <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>object<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
        <span class="pl-ent">"description"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Schema for a flight-related request.<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
  <span class="pl-ent">"properties"</span>: {
            <span class="pl-ent">"action"</span>: { <span class="pl-ent">"$ref"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>#/components/schemas/FlightAction<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> }
        }
      },
      <span class="pl-ent">"FlightAction"</span>: {
      <span class="pl-ent">"type"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>string<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>,
          <span class="pl-ent">"enum"</span>: [<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>search<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>book<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>cancel<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>]
      }
    }
  }
}</pre></div>

  <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c"><!--</span> Reference schemas using a namespace and JSON Pointer <span class="pl-c">--></span></span>

              <span class="pl-e">event</span><span class="pl-e">:</span><span class=
